name: Buffer

name: Boundary
description: Boundary is a Geoprocessing Activity that returns a polygon containing the vertecies of an input geometry without any interoir rings

name: Envelope
description: Envelope is a Geoprocessing Activity that returns the smallest rectangle with sides parallel to the coordinate axes that contains all the vertecies of an input geometry

name: Bounding Circle
description: Bounding Circle is a Geoprocessing Activity that returns the smallest circle that contains all the vertecies of an input geometry

name: Concave Hull
description: Concave Hull is a Geoprocessing Activity that returns the smallest concave polygon containing all the vertecies in an input geometry, unless the number of vertecies in the input geometry is less than three. For two points, the concave hull collapses to a line; for one, a point.

name: Convex Hull
description: Convex Hull is a Geoprocessing Activity that returns the smallest convex polygon containing all the vertecies in an input geometry, unless the number of vertecies in the input geometry is less than three. For two points, the concave hull collapses to a line; for one, a point.

name: Regression

name: SEN2SR

name: Mosaic

name: NDVI

name: Best available pixel (BAP)

name: D8 flow-direction derivation
description: Assigns each elevation-raster cell a flow direction toward the steepest downslope neighbour among its eight surrounding cells.

name: D8 flow-accumulation derivation
description: Calculates the accumulated upstream contribution for each cell by following an input D8 flow-direction raster.

name: Watershed/catchment delineation
description: Identifies the raster cells or polygon area draining to a specified outlet, using a flow-direction or flow-accumulation model.

name: Stream-network extraction
description: Identifies likely stream cells or stream features from a flow-accumulation raster using a specified contributing-area threshold.

name: Distance-to-feature calculation
description: Calculates the shortest distance from each raster cell to the nearest input feature, such as a stream or other vector or raster feature.

name: Zonal raster statistics
description: Calculates summary statistics, such as mean, median, minimum or maximum, for raster cells within each input polygon or grid zone.

name: Raster sampling at points
description: Extracts the value of an input raster, or a defined neighbourhood of raster cells, at each input point location.

name: DGGS cell indexing
description: Quantizes input spatial positions or geometries to cells at a specified resolution in a Discrete Global Grid System and returns the corresponding cell identifiers.

name: FAS Source Fetch
description: External catalog API pull. Retrieves source records from an authoritative external endpoint via a Voyager HQ Python connector, generating raw source records as the connector-chain start.

name: FAS Code Decode
description: Numeric-code → human-readable-string lookup against a compiled taxonomy. Turns FAS unit IDs, attribute IDs, and ISO country codes into descriptive fields.

name: FAS Geolocate
description: Country / place-name → GeoJSON geometry lookup via a gazetteer service. Terminal step of the connector chain; produces the indexed-doc entity that bridges to the pipeline chain.

name: NLP Entity Extraction
description: Named-entity recognition over document text. Emits structured entity mentions (persons, organizations, places, events, products). Semantically upstream of Geotag.

name: Geotag
description: Place-name mention → coordinate lookup. Consumes the place mentions produced by NLP Entity Extraction and resolves each against an external gazetteer. Produces spatial features from text-derived input, complementing pixel-derived geometry ops.

name: Commodity Classification
description: Text → commodity-taxonomy classifier (dictionary matcher over normalized labels). Domain-specific to agricultural / commodity data.

name: Region Classification
description: Text → region-taxonomy classifier. Emitted in the pipeline for canonical region classification and cross-repository tagging.

name: Field Normalization
description: Field concatenation / normalization to a common schema across heterogeneous inputs. Produces uniform fields for downstream indexing and retrieval.

name: Retrieve
description: Hybrid Solr search over the enriched index (semantic + lexical). Emitted by the mastra voyager-search tool as the first activity of a Retrieval-Augmented Generation cycle.

name: Generate
description: LLM answer synthesis over retrieved chunks. Terminal step of a Retrieval-Augmented Generation workflow; produces the natural-language answer plus a PROV bundle citation trail.

name: Text Metadata Enrichment
description: Umbrella Geoprocessing Activity type for pipeline-side operations that extract, classify, geotag, and normalize document metadata for downstream discovery. Groups NLP Entity Extraction, Geotag, Commodity Classification, Region Classification, Field Normalization.

name: Retrieval-Augmented Generation
description: Umbrella Geoprocessing Activity type for RAG-layer operations that retrieve indexed content and synthesize answers using an LLM, producing PROV-traceable outputs. Groups Retrieve, Generate.

name: Outputs a monoband image which is the result of a mathematical operation on several multi-band images.
description: This application performs a mathematical operation on several multi-band images and outputs the result into a monoband image. The given expression is computed at each pixel position. Evaluation of the mathematical formula is done by the muParser library.The formula can be written using:* numerical values ( 2.3, -5, 3.1e4, ...)* variables containing pixel values (e.g. ``im2b3`` is the pixel value in 2nd image, 3rd band)* binary operators: * ``+`` addition, ``-`` subtraction, ``*`` multiplication, ``/`` division * ``^`` raise x to the power of y * ``

name: This application performs mathematical operations on several multiband images.
description: This application performs a mathematical operation on several multi-band images and outputs the result into an image (multi- or mono-band, as opposed to the BandMath OTB-application). The mathematical formula is done by the muParserX library.The list of features and the syntax of muParserX is available at [1].As opposed to muParser (and thus the BandMath OTB-application [2]), muParserX supports vector expressions which allows outputting multi-band images.Hereafter is a brief reference of the muParserX syntaxFundamentals------------The formula can be written using:* numerical values ( 2.3, -5, 3.1e4, ...)* variables containing pixel values (please, note the indexing of inputs from 1 to N). Examples for the first input image: * ``im1`` a pixel from 1st input, made of n components (n bands) * ``im1b2`` the 2nd component of a pixel from 1st input (band index is 1-based) * ``im1b2N3x4`` a 3x4 pixels Neighbourhood of a pixel the 2nd component of a pixel from the 1st input * ``im1PhyX`` horizontal (X-axis) spacing of the 1st input. * ``im1PhyY`` vertical (Y-axis) spacing of the 1st input input. * ``im1b2Mean`` mean of the 2nd component of the 1st input (global statistics) * ``im1b2Mini`` minimum of the 2nd component of the 1st input (global statistics) * ``im1b2Maxi`` maximum of the 2nd component of the 1st input (global statistics) * ``im1b2Sum`` sum of the 2nd component of the 1st input (global statistics) * ``im1b2Var`` variance of the 2nd component of the 1st input (global statistics) * ``idxX`` and ``idxY`` are the indices of the current pixel (generic variables)* binary operators: * ``+`` addition, ``-`` subtraction, ``*`` multiplication, ``/`` division * ``^`` raise x to the power of y * ``

name: Extract a ROI defined by the user.
description: This application extracts a Region Of Interest with user parameters. There are four mode of extraction. The standard mode allows the user to enter one point (upper left corner of the region to extract) and a size. The extent mode needs two points (upper left corner and lower right) and the radius mode need the center of the region and the radius: it will extract the rectangle containing the circle defined and limited by the image dimension. The fit mode needs a reference image or vector and the dimension of the extracted region will be the same as the extent of the reference. Different units are available such as pixel, image physical space or longitude and latitude.

name: Analytical Hillshading
description: This tool performs an analytical hillshade computation for an elevation grid. The 'Standard' method simply calculates the angle at which light coming from the position of the light source would hit the surface. This method can produce angles greater than 90 degree. With the second method all values are kept within the range of 0-90 degree. It can be enhanced with shadowing effects, where shadowed cells will be marked with a value of exactly 90 degree. 'Shadows Only' creates a mask for the shadowed areas and sets all other cells to no-data. 'Combined Shading' takes the values of the standard method and multiplies these with the normalized slope. 'Ambient Occlusion' is based on the concepts of Tarini et al. (2006), but only the northern half-space is considered here.
